key_insight: A proposed fault-tolerant quantum processor replaces per-qubit external control with a fixed, clocked local circuit and a constant number of instruction wires.
engineering_relevance: The architecture could reduce external wiring and control complexity while supporting universal quantum computation.
method: Move quantum information through a planar array using a fixed, periodically applied, geometrically local depth-3 circuit.
Inject classical instructions through a constant number of external wires, each attached to one qubit.
Prove an accuracy threshold for noisy gates, measurements, and wires under a noiseless global clock.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical threshold theorem, not hardware experiments: n physical qubits support n/polylog(n/ε) logical qubits at logical-gate error rate ε.
watch_item: The noiseless-clock assumption is idealized, and the fully local design takes n/polylog(n/ε) time per logical gate; faster operation requires instantaneous noiseless on-chip classical broadcasts.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
